chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi Maryam al-Ansari, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: concerning

Regarding two men who joined together in cutting off a man's hand, he عليه السلام said: "If he wishes to have both of their hands cut off, he pays to them the compensation of one hand, and they divide it between themselves; then he cuts off both of their hands. And if he wishes, he may take from them the compensation of one hand." He عليه السلام said: "And if he cuts off one of them, then the one whose hand was not cut off must return to the one whose hand was cut off one quarter of the compensation."

key_terms.اِجْتَمَعَا: acted together jointly in committing the injury
key_terms.دِيَةَ: monetary compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.رُبُعَ الدِّيَةِ: one quarter of the prescribed blood-compensation
key_terms.قَطْعِ: severing or cutting off of a limb
key_terms.يَدِ: the hand that was injured or subject to legal retaliation
key_terms.يَقْطَعُهُمَا: he carries out qisas by cutting off both of their hands

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two men jointly cut off one man's hand in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for two offenders who jointly sever a man's hand. The injured person may either take the diyah of one hand from them, or seek qisas against both under the stated financial adjustment; and if only one is subjected to qisas, the other owes a quarter of the diyah to him.
